clue.text: Iron prominent in compelling African investment scene

indicators.note: something prominent in a thing stands out in its midst, so the metal symbol sits inside the other word

parts.note: making someone do something is compelling them
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A strong iron feature dominates a gripping scene of investment in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' is the military sense, a siege: Mafeking in South Africa was famously besieged in the Boer War. 'Investment' tempts a financial reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The town was the site of a celebrated siege, and to invest a town is to besiege it.

clue.text: Clean up domestic animal, a little one

parts.note: to mop is to clean up a floor or spill
a pet is a domestic animal kept for company

explanation.surface: Wipe up after the household pet, a small one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an affectionate term for a small child, a little tot.

clue.text: Minor skin irritations caused by jumpers

definitions.text: Minor skin irritations caused by jumpers

parts.words: Minor skin irritations caused by jumpers
parts.note: the jumpers are not woollen sweaters but leaping insects whose bites itch

explanation.surface: Woollen sweaters can make the skin itch slightly.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is British for a sweater, so the surface suggests itchy wool; the jumpers are leaping insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Small itchy marks left by bites of a leaping parasite are trivial annoyances in both senses.

clue.text: Guarding gate before midnight

indicators.note: before means the first piece comes ahead of the next

parts.note: to gate a pupil is to confine them as a punishment, to keep in
the middle letter of the word night is G

explanation.surface: A watchman guards the gate until twelve at night.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something is protecting or watching over it, as in safe keeping.

clue.text: Hard to find in seaside resort the right place?

indicators.note: something to be found in a word is placed inside it

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is hard to find the right spot at a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a position exactly suited to someone, the right slot for them.

clue.text: Models misbehaving infrequently

indicators.note: letters that misbehave will not stay in their proper order, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fashion models rarely behave badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean rarely, not often.

clue.text: Passed English, and failed thereafter

indicators.note: thereafter means the second piece comes after the first

parts.note: a policy or habit that lapsed failed or fell away

explanation.surface: A student passed in English and then failed later.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' looks like exam success, but it is time going by. 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has gone by, slipped away.

clue.text: Bishop housed in expensive block

indicators.note: a piece housed in another is put inside it

parts.note: dear means costly, expensive
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop lives in a costly block of flats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'block' tempts as a noun, a building; it is the verb, to bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to prevent or exclude them, to stop them taking part.

clue.text: Harbour dockage extremely steep

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for yachts

indicators.note: extremely takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of the word dockage

explanation.surface: Harbour charges for docking are exorbitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steep' reads as costly; it is the verb, to soak.
explanation.definitionFit: Food steeped in a seasoned liquid is soaked in a marinade to absorb its flavour.

clue.text: A bit of neck and singular resolution to traverse steep rock

indicators.note: to traverse something is to stretch across it, so the outer pieces span the rock

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an end is a purpose or aim, what one resolves to achieve
a crag is a steep rugged rock

explanation.surface: A climber needs a bit of neck and single-minded resolve to cross a steep rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' suggests nerve, but it is a cut of meat: the scrag end is the bony neck of mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: This cheap cut is the bony neck of mutton or lamb, a piece of the neck.

clue.text: Honoured companion enters bearing colour in royal reception area

indicators.note: one piece going into the join of two others is said to enter them

parts.note: a person's bearing or demeanour is their presence
amber is a yellowish-orange colour
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A distinguished guest walks into a royal reception room bearing a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'enters' puts the companion between the two words, not inside one.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace room where a monarch receives visitors in person is so called.

clue.text: Recession that shows up more in the Strand

definitions.text: Recession that shows up more in the Strand

parts.words: Recession that shows up more in the Strand
parts.note: a strand is a shore, and when the sea recedes more of the beach is exposed

explanation.surface: An economic downturn that is most visible in London's famous street, the Strand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a London street, so 'recession' reads as economic; here it is the sea going out from a strand, a shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The outflowing of the sea is a recession of water that uncovers more of the shore.

clue.text: Item published is not a winner

parts.note: item is Latin for likewise, an old word for also when listing
a newspaper that ran a story published it

explanation.surface: A news item that was published failed to win any prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or contestant placed outside the top finishers is a mere loser in the race.

clue.text: Lose incentive to act in National Theatre going round

indicators.note: one piece going round another surrounds it, so the theatre word holds the other

parts.note: the stage is the theatre as a profession
Nat. is an abbreviation for national

explanation.surface: Someone loses their drive to perform at the National Theatre on tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'National Theatre' looks like one name, but the two words are separate pieces, and 'to act' belongs to the definition. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagnate is to become inactive or sluggish, losing the impetus to move.

clue.text: Publicize skill in making Wellingtons, say

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public
craft means skill or art

explanation.surface: Advertise the skill of making wellington boots.
explanation.walkthrough: Wellingtons are rubber boots, but here the Vickers Wellington, a Second World War bomber. 'in making' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vickers Wellington was a bomber, so several of them are examples of planes.

clue.text: Daughter keen to meet this handsome youth?

parts.note: keen and avid both mean eager

explanation.surface: An eager daughter wants to meet this good-looking young man.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Michelangelo's statue of the young biblical hero, an icon of male beauty. 'to meet' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Michelangelo's famous marble statue shows the shepherd boy as an ideal of youthful beauty.

clue.text: Shiver and shake — put on a top coat

indicators.note: shaken letters are jumbled, so these come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone shivers and shakes, so puts on an overcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top coat' reads as an overcoat; it is the final coat of finish on wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood that has been given a glossy protective final layer has had its finishing coat applied.

clue.text: Friendly, and remaining so if caught out

definitions.text: Friendly, and remaining so if caught out

parts.words: Friendly, and remaining so if caught out
parts.note: caught is C in cricket, and with that letter taken out the word left still means friendly

explanation.surface: Someone stays good-natured even when caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C (caught) and AMIABLE remains, also meaning friendly, so the clue is a definition plus a description of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and peaceable, as in an amicable settlement.

clue.text: Endless unhappiness for one of the nearest

indicators.note: endless means with the last letter cut off this synonym

parts.note: misery means great unhappiness

explanation.surface: Endless misery afflicts one of those closest to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearest' is the old sense of near, stingy, not closest in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean mean with money, so the nearest are the stingiest people, like a skinflint.

clue.text: King in a state, Egyptian

parts.note: the state is Egypt, and the clue describes one of its pharaohs

explanation.surface: A king from an Egyptian state.
explanation.walkthrough: Several pharaohs bore this name, the best known Rameses II.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of several ancient pharaohs, kings who ruled the Nile kingdom.

clue.text: Sort of setter needed to flush game bird

parts.note: the red setter is a breed of gundog
to flush game is to start it, driving birds from cover

explanation.surface: A gundog is needed to drive the game birds out of cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game bird' reads as one phrase, but 'game' belongs with 'flush' and 'bird' alone is the definition. 'needed to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This small thrush with a reddish tail is a songbird of woods and gardens.

clue.text: Youthful driver's accessory to mount on front of engine

parts.note: a golfer using a driver places the ball on a tee
a nag is a horse, something to mount

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter, so take the opening letter of engine

explanation.surface: A young motorist fits an accessory to the front of the engine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driver' suggests a motorist; it is a golf club. 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage means relating to youth between thirteen and nineteen.

clue.text: Cheque's presenter not so well covered, according to auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners here, so the word is one heard rather than seen

parts.note: barer means more naked, less well clothed

explanation.surface: A cheque is presented by someone less well insured, the accountants say.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors suggest accountants, but here they are hearers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheque made out to the holder is payable to whoever presents it.

clue.text: Might her spelling leave something to be desired?

definitions.text: Might her spelling leave something to be desired?

parts.words: Might her spelling leave something to be desired?
parts.note: spelling here means casting spells, and the person who casts them makes herself desirable

explanation.surface: A woman's poor spelling may fall short of the standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave something to be desired' usually means falls short; here her spells literally leave someone desiring her.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanting, attractive person casts a spell over others and makes herself desired.

clue.text: Engineers brought in to help in broadcast

indicators.note: letters brought in to another word are placed inside it

parts.note: aid means help
RE stands for the Royal Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: Engineers were brought in to assist with a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that was broadcast went out over the airwaves, was transmitted.

clue.text: Direct flight in business class by busy worker

indicators.note: by means beside, so one piece sits next to the other

parts.note: the bee is the proverbial busy worker
a line is a class of business or trade, as in his line of work

explanation.surface: Someone flies straight to their destination in business class, seated by a hard worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business class' tempts as an airline cabin; here it is a line of business. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a straight course, as a bee is said to fly straight home to its hive.

clue.text: Fan meeting old comic actor

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fan

explanation.surface: A fan meets an old comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: In opera a buffo is a singer of comic roles, a comedian on the stage.

clue.text: Awfully bored with the affairs of proverbially flighty assembly

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so these letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: A gathering of flighty people is terribly bored by the business at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'of' are link words; the fodder is BORED and THE AFFAIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says such birds flock together, so the phrase names a group of like-minded people.

clue.text: Yield estate in part for the first-born

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of an estate is surrendered to the first-born child.
explanation.definitionFit: The oldest child of a family is the firstborn.

clue.text: Strange order to a ring fighter

indicators.note: strange means odd or unusual, so these letters take on an unusual order

explanation.surface: An odd instruction is given to a boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' suggests boxing; it is the bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter fights in the bullring, so is a fighter in a ring.
